recognize_zh: 周邊血液中一群母細胞，胞質深藍且邊緣有泡狀突起（cytoplasmic blebs），部分核呈不規則或凹陷，旁邊還可見有核紅血球；這種帶胞質突起的母細胞是巨核母細胞（megakaryoblast）的典型線索，配合唐氏症背景即 ML-DS。
features: Cluster of medium to large blasts with high N:C ratio and moderately condensed to fine chromatin
Deeply basophilic cytoplasm with irregular borders and cytoplasmic blebs/pseudopod-like projections
Some blasts with indented or folded nuclei; cytoplasm agranular with pale vacuolated zones
Circulating nucleated red cell (orthochromatic normoblast) at lower left
Background red cells with mild anisopoikilocytosis
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a cluster of circulating blasts. The blasts are medium to large with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios, round to indented nuclei, relatively fine chromatin, and deeply basophilic agranular cytoplasm with prominent cytoplasmic blebs and irregular projections. A nucleated red blood cell is present, and red cells show mild anisopoikilocytosis. The blast morphology suggests megakaryoblastic differentiation; in a patient with Down syndrome, findings are consistent with myeloid leukemia associated with Down syndrome (acute megakaryoblastic type), to be confirmed by flow cytometry for CD41/CD61 and GATA1 mutation studies.

ddx.vs: TAM blasts are morphologically identical megakaryoblasts, so the distinction is clinical: TAM presents in the neonatal period (usually <3 months) and regresses spontaneously, whereas ML-DS arises later, typically before age 5.
Lymphoblasts lack cytoplasmic blebbing and are CD19 or cCD3 positive, whereas megakaryoblasts express CD41/CD61.
Monoblasts have more abundant gray-blue cytoplasm with fine granules and nonspecific esterase positivity, while megakaryoblasts are NSE-negative and platelet glycoprotein positive.
